findings.claim: In the UK, copyright in a photograph, film or written work typically lasts for the creator's lifetime plus 70 years.
findings.truth: Written and artistic works, including photographs, usually last 70 years after the creator dies. A film's term depends on the last surviving director, screenplay author or composer, rather than one creator.

findings.claim: BBFC 12A/12, 15 and 18 certificates carry legal force for cinema admissions.
findings.truth: For cinema admission, the relevant age restrictions are 12A, 15 and 18. The 12 classification is for home entertainment releases.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, British Board of Film Classification and Video Recordings Act summaries (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Media creators working with children must also ensure parental consent is obtained before recording or publishing any content featuring under-18s.
findings.truth: Consent is one of several lawful bases under UK GDPR; it is not a blanket requirement for all content featuring under-18s. For identifiable content, creators should identify the lawful basis and follow safeguarding procedures.
findings.evidence: ICO, Lawful basis and Consent guidance (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: When submitting coursework for this unit, students must produce pre-production documents including visualisation diagrams as evidence of planning before they begin creating their final product.
findings.truth: R093 is externally assessed. Students need to understand planning documents and their uses, but the specification excludes creating them from scratch.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1, R093 assessment; spec 4.2, Topic Area 3.3

findings.claim: Screen resolution is typically 72–96 PPI; print requires at least 300 DPI.
findings.truth: For screen delivery, pixel dimensions and rendering context matter; there is no universal 72–96 PPI file requirement. 300 DPI is a common print-production guideline, not a specification-wide minimum. Options: replace the repeated fixed-value rule with output-context guidance and revise its checks, or retain the figures only as qualified house guidance. This would need coordinated changes across content, practice questions, checks, flashcards and glossary.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2.1; W3C CSS Values and Units Level 4, screen pixel and reference-pixel guidance (fetched 2026-09-04)

summary: Four verified, surgical corrections were prepared for lessons 5 and 6. Lesson 9 needs a coordinated editorial decision rather than a partial correction.
